He kept every draft
which sounds like sentimentality but was closer to bookkeeping.
When a passage stopped working he could go back and find the version
before the damage
and often the fault turned out to be a small decision made three
revisions earlier for reasons he had long since forgotten.
Without the record he would have rewritten the same mistake, patiently
for years.
Translation is less about words than about what a sentence is doing.
A joke that turns on a pun must become a joke that turns on something
else
or it stops being a joke
and a formal register that signals distance in one language may signal
nothing at all in another.
The translator who preserves every word and loses the effect has
produced an accurate document and a failed piece of writing.
